introHeading: The 360 booth, built for Williamsburg's rooftops and loft parties
introParas: The 360 booth works differently from the mirror or glam booth we set up elsewhere in Williamsburg — instead of a print, guests walk away with a video, shot from every angle as the camera arm sweeps around the platform. On a Wythe or Kent Avenue rooftop, that arm has the Manhattan skyline behind it for the whole rotation, which is a big part of why this is the booth Williamsburg's younger, share-happy crowds ask for by name. The equipment itself is sturdier outdoors than it looks — the platform and arm are built to run outside, not just tolerate it — but we still check for a level surface and enough clearance overhead before we commit to a rooftop spot.

Because the arm sweeps a full circle, the 360 needs more room than most of what we bring to the neighborhood: 8ft x 8ft minimum, 12ft x 12ft where the roof deck or loft floor allows it, with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance so the arm has a clean pass. That last number is rarely a problem in the converted industrial buildings off Berry Street, where the same tall ceilings that suit a warehouse party suit this booth. The platform breaks down for a single freight-elevator trip, so moving it from a rooftop bar down into an East Williamsburg loft after-party doesn't mean a second load-in from scratch — and it wants its own dedicated 15 or 20 amp outlet, worth flagging early if your rooftop bar's power is already split between the DJ and the bar setup.

Setup takes about 20 minutes and we arrive a full hour ahead of your start time to test the arm before anyone's watching. There is no travel fee anywhere in Williamsburg — it's minutes from us, and we quote everything from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: Does the 360 booth work on a Wythe or Kent Avenue rooftop?
faqs.a: Yes — it's one of the most-requested rooftop bookings we run in the neighborhood. We check for a level surface, a wind-sheltered position and enough overhead clearance for the arm's full sweep before confirming the spot, and we'll scout access and power with you ahead of the date.

faqs.q: Can the platform fit into a Berry Street or East Williamsburg loft through a freight elevator?
faqs.a: Yes. The 360 breaks down for a single freight-elevator trip, which is the standard load-in for the converted industrial spaces off Berry — useful if your event moves from a rooftop bar into an indoor after-party on the same night.

faqs.q: How much floor space does the 360 booth need?
faqs.a: 8ft x 8ft is the minimum, 12ft x 12ft where the room or roof deck allows it, with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for the arm to complete its sweep. Most Williamsburg loft spaces off Berry and Kent clear that without issue.

faqs.q: What power does the 360 booth need at a Williamsburg venue?
faqs.a: A dedicated 15 or 20 amp outlet, ideally not shared with the DJ or bar setup. Rooftop bars in particular tend to run tighter circuits than a loft floor, so tell us about your venue's power and we'll plan the placement around it.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee to bring the 360 booth to Williamsburg?
faqs.a: No travel fee — Williamsburg is minutes from us. We quote everything from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: Is the 360 booth good for a Williamsburg wedding or milestone birthday?
faqs.a: Yes, especially for a younger guest list that will share the clip before the night's over. For a more traditional, multigenerational Williamsburg wedding we usually point couples to the mirror booth instead — ask us and we'll tell you honestly which fits your guest list.

faqs.q: Can the 360 booth be branded for a corporate event?
faqs.a: Yes — the platform, the video overlay, the intro and outro frames and the sharing screen can all carry your logo and colors, which is common for the brand activations and product launches we run in Williamsburg's event spaces.

faqs.q: How long does setup take, and can you arrive early for a rooftop event?
faqs.a: About 20 minutes once we're on site, and we build in a full hour before your scheduled start time to test the arm before guests arrive. If your rooftop needs us there earlier for an access window, idle time runs $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance and can you provide a COI for a Williamsburg venue?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million insurance policy. If your venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact email and we will send it over.

faqs.q: Which Williamsburg neighborhoods do you cover?
faqs.a: We're out across North Williamsburg, South Williamsburg, East Williamsburg, Wythe Avenue, Berry Street, Kent Avenue and the surrounding areas most weekends of the season. If your venue isn't on that list, ask anyway — we'll tell you honestly whether we can get there.
